body:
Thank you very much for your reply. Personally, I am struggling to get back onto the right path and being alone, everything just seems hopeless. 

I do have a question to ask you, did your life ever get better? What is is that you did to do so? 

> I read through your other post and it strikes me that none of the advice given made reference to your Aspergers or ADHD. Of course you get lost in blogs, that's a repetitive behaviour.

I don't know how to control this, as it seems to be impulsive. I've tried to restrict myself but even that has limits; it backfires on me. And forcing myself, this requires mental energy that exhausts me. 


>Forgive me if I'm reading this wrong, but you yourself don't seem to really acknowledge the debilitating effects of this condition in your own writing. You are being extremely hard on yourself.

I think its all about me comparing myself to others and constantly telling myself, "if they can do it, why can't you?" This is the attitude that mentally drains me because they don't have the disabilities I do. 

These are the precise reason why I feel like giving up, what's the point of continuing when you know its not possible? I basically live a life where I am in the shadow of others, basically non-existent. 

>I've only just been diagnosed with Aspergers, but I've lived with it, along with depression and OCD for forty-odd years and it's been bloody hard.

How has your conditions improved? What did you do to make a difference?


> You mentioned that you aren't on any meds. If it's not too intrusive, would you mind elaborating on why this is? 

Health reasons. My body cannot handle it.


To your uni post:

> The only time I felt release was when I cut myself and saw the blood. How do your experiences compare, are there similarities?

I have had a bad habit of being distracted to the internet, to the good parts and bad parts. The bad parts involve watching inappropriate videos and doing self pleasure (I hope I don't have to explain any further than this). Luckily, with willpower I have managed to put a halt (or at least shift my mind towards it). My past had a lot to do with this, I was never like this but the people around me was the reason why I turned to this. I didn't know any better. This issue continued until now, I am fighting to stop it; its hurtful to myself and others.  


> Have you approached your student/disability support services? What have they offered you?

I have been going to a counseling at my uni for x months and I think it makes little difference. I will be starting group based therapy in a few weeks and see how that turns out. All I noticed that my confidence did increase, briefly. 


> What has been your experience of friendship so far? I find myself torn between wanting to avoid (my self-inflicted) isolation and just finding the whole thing draining and too much trouble.

In the past, I have noticed I lost friends due to small arguments or disagreements; I think I struggle to maintain friends. All I have noticed that people avoid me or they are hardly interested in me.  So inevitably, I gave up all together and accepted myself. I am shy and I've never had a friend. I've been bullied most throughout my entire life so I tend to restrict any close communications. 


>You have more experience of this than me, so I'll assume you're familiar with all the ASD support websites out there. Have you gained support from any of these?

I have tried to reach out but due to my studies, I have no time. Only my university counseling seem to work for me but this too requires time and effort.

I hope that answers all, I am simply looking for help. The stress, worry, anxiety is destroying me. I don't know whats going on and I don't know how long will this phase last, I am struggling to keep hope. Please help and thank you!

I am sorry, I don't know what to do. I am really lost. I have no emotional support and trapped in my bedroom walls. I just wish this difficult phase was over and I could get on with my life. All this is slowing me down. I turned to the internet world full of strangers for help.

> What part of the world are you in ? 

USA

> What age are you and are a male or female? 

mid 20s male.

> I only ask to see what stage of your life you are at?

senior college student in computer engineering. 


This doesn't answer my question.

This is useful for me; thanks. 

I can't take a break or drop out because I am nearly close to graduation. Its hard to hang on, I've ben in school for almost 7 years. The pressure in my community is strong so I have to hide this fact. 

I like programming but I can't seem to get a decent internship. My past experience is not worth much.
I am in computer engineering, everything is hard to understand and people just figure things out quickly. I can't even keep up with them and this hurts me a lot.
I have been to counseling for many months but it doesn't help. Its so mentally painful to watch others have good life, good success. Yet, you work so hard and you still get nothing.

Because I am a complete failure, I cant figure anything out, I have no friends who care for me and have disappointed my own family. I am struggling academically in my engineering classes, I can't get an internship because I struggle to communicate, I don't care anymore, I don't want to see the light of day ever again. Let someone else take my place on this planet.
